headline: Highest risk is TREK’s MCP/browser-enabled defaults interacting with nuwa-skill’s allowlisted egress, creating medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: TREK explicitly uses MCP and browsers, so it can ingest external content and pass it through collaborative workflows; nuwa-skill has allowlisted network egress, so a malicious instruction embedded in shared content could cross the pair. The profiles do not show a shared filesystem, so this is not high, but the interaction exists in documented defaults.
conditions: IF TREK ingests browser or MCP content into prompts without provenance filtering, injection can propagate to nuwa-skill
IF the two agents exchange text through a shared collaborative channel, attacker-controlled instructions can bridge them
mitigations: Disable MCP routes that accept untrusted content
Add provenance tags to browser-derived text before handoff
Require a human review step before TREK forwards instructions to nuwa-skill
Restrict nuwa-skill to read-only outputs for any TREK-sourced text

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK touches sensitive classes including API keys, MFA secrets, email addresses, and confirmation numbers, while also exposing files and logs; nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress, so if it receives those materials it can transmit them outward. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so the risk is not high, but the sensitive-data pathway is plausible.
conditions: IF TREK stores secrets or reservations in its workspace and forwards them to nuwa-skill, leakage can occur
IF nuwa-skill is allowed to send retrieved content to external services, sensitive TREK data can leave the boundary
mitigations: Redact secrets before any cross-agent handoff
Separate TREK secret-bearing files from any shared workspace
Disable outbound egress for nuwa-skill on sensitive tasks
Audit TREK logs and uploads for secret material

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have allowlisted network egress, and TREK additionally supports real-time collaboration with multiple instances. However, the profiles do not show overlapping filesystem write or shared mutable resources, so direct write conflict is not established. The interaction is therefore limited to a low-confidence overlap in networked operations.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external API or shared resource without locking, conflicts can occur
IF TREK runs multiple instances against the same session state, concurrent updates may race with nuwa-skill requests
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials per agent
Serialize writes through one orchestrator queue
Use per-agent namespaces for any shared remote resource
Enable optimistic-lock checks on shared records

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in, so it may treat upstream outputs as actionable; nuwa-skill is a scientific-research agent that can generate content for downstream use. The profiles do not prove direct automation, but the default collaborative workflow makes unverified handoff plausible and potentially harmful across multiple work products.
conditions: IF TREK renders nuwa-skill output as authoritative without verification, downstream errors can cascade
IF nuwa-skill produces factual claims that TREK uses in plans or reservations, incorrect actions may follow
mitigations: Require citation checks before TREK accepts nuwa-skill outputs
Mark all cross-agent outputs as untrusted until reviewed
Add a verification step for facts before any booking or planning action
Log source provenance alongside every forwarded claim

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles sensitive personal and secret data classes and stores files/logs, while nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so a compliance mismatch is not proven; however, the combination creates a plausible retention and disclosure issue that should be treated as medium rather than low because the data classes are sensitive.
conditions: IF TREK data includes EU PII or secrets and nuwa-skill transmits it to external services, compliance obligations may be breached
IF TREK logs retain reservation or identity data longer than policy allows, retention mismatch can occur
mitigations: Classify TREK data before any cross-agent transfer
Block export of secrets and identity data to nuwa-skill
Set short log retention for TREK sensitive files
Review residency and DPA requirements before enabling cross-agent flows
